title: Distinct finite-temperature phase diagrams of non-invertible Kennedy--Tasaki duals
summary: Do two Hamiltonians related by a non-invertible transformation necessarily share the same finite-temperature phase diagram? For a cluster-model interpolation $H(s)$ and its Kennedy--Tasaki dual $\tilde H(s)$, the map is a partial isometry and equates only their all-plus-sector partition functions. In one dimension, thermal order is forbidden on both sides, leaving only the common zero-temperature transition at $s=\tfrac12$.
